correctness.rationale: For prime squares, coprimality to p rules out the required divisibility. For pq with p=2, reduction mod q+1 gives q+1|4 and q=3. For odd p<q the exact equivalence AB|pq(A-1)(B-1), with A=(p+1)/2 and B=(q+1)/2, yields B|p(A-1) and A|B-1. Since B>A and gcd(p,A-1)=1, B=pd for d|A-1; reduction modulo A forces d=A-1. The converse holds because gcd(A,B)=1, B|p(A-1), A|B-1. Computation is only corroboration.
